newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil lower on futures, but premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil lower on futures, but premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended lower on Thursday after benchmark IPE futures fell on profit-taking and lack of fresh supportative news, although traders said premiums were stready amid good demand and tightish supply.
A prompt DIN cargo was reported, but not confirmed, done at the equivalent of Oct IPE +9.0, cif Hamburg.

Traders second half September DIN was scarce. Further out the market was talking Oct IPE +$7/+$7.50 for Oct 1-10 delivery. Low sulphur premiums were steady. Into Germany they were put at Oct +$16/+$17, although a 5,000 tonne prompt cargo was done into Hamburg at Oct IPE +$18 on Wednesday. The spectre of some 500,000 tonnes of north American gas oil loomed over the market, although many traders said most of it was bound for the Mediterranean and that French and German demand would easily swallow any extra supply.
"I don't think the first October batch of cargoes will be a problem, but the arb's still open and if cargoes keep coming we could see some pressure," said one trader.
On the barge market, traders said the market was very quiet with heating oil offered at Oct IPE +$10.
